publisher: Aarhus University – Economics and Business Administration (Herning)
claim: AU publishes the current programme, campus, subject requirements, quota criteria and historical 2026 cutoffs.
excerpt: English B; Mathematics B; History B, History of Ideas B, Social Science B, Contemporary History B or International Economics B. The Danish programme page states a 6.0 overall GPA floor for quota 1; this English page omits it. Quota 2 uses those subject grades plus documented relevant qualifications; the expectation-matching meeting is optional. 2026 cutoff 6.9, standby 6; English, Herning. Historical top-up text is not current first-year entry.
interpretation: The English page's omission is not an exemption. The exact Danish quota-1 source is recorded separately as ev-dk-au-herning-quota1-danish-20261030 and referenced by the requirement.

claim: AU requires the Diploma with 24 points or the supplemented Course Results route, uses results service code 000150 for same-year IB results, and excludes same-year paying IB candidates.
excerpt: Structured restatement: apply by 15 March noon. Already completed diplomas are uploaded with the application. Same-year candidates authorise AU through IBNET results service code 000150 and retain the receipt; other documents are due 5 July noon. Retake candidates also upload their original Course Results and state the retake. Paying applicants must have their final qualification by 15 March noon and cannot apply in the year they earn the IB. AU accepts Global Politics HL as Social Science B, or Global Politics SL with Economics SL/HL. AU still mentions HF-enkeltfag or GSK for Course Results; the national authority expressly excludes GSK for raising the qualification itself.
interpretation: Retain the national recognition-body route and flag the conflict. An AU reference to GSK must not override the national distinction between qualification-level supplementation and meeting a programme subject requirement.

publisher: Aarhus University – Deadlines and important dates
claim: AU sets annual application/document, quota 2, reply and conditional-supplementation deadlines; these have no published intake year.
excerpt: Structured restatement: 1 February portal opens. 15 March noon CET: international/IB applications, signature page, quota 2 documents, paying-applicant qualifying examination and English test, and application fee. 5 July noon: general qualifying examination, English test or registration and supplementary course or summer-course enrolment. 28 July ordinary answer. 3 August accept through MyApplication. 5 September final conditional-supplementary evidence. Page revised 24 August 2026; annual day/month dates remain provisional for 2027.

publisher: Aarhus University – Tuition fees and application fee
claim: For applications after 1 November 2026 AU no longer refunds the EUR 150 application fee and requires first-year tuition before the first semester; EU/EEA/Swiss and listed residence exemptions remain.
excerpt: Structured restatement: EU/EEA/Swiss citizens pay no tuition or application fee. Other applicants must check AU’s listed residence exemptions. EUR 150 application fee per paying applicant is due 15 March; for applications after 1 November 2026 it is not refunded on enrolment. First-year tuition is paid in full before semester start; later payments are per semester. No bachelor scholarships. Paying applicants need their final diploma and transcripts by 15 March noon; no same-year IB entry. The paying-applicant definition mentions no permanent Danish address, while the application-fee section omits that address condition: applicants with a Danish address should confirm classification with AU.
interpretation: The future-effective refund/payment change covers autumn 2027 applications. Do not assume every non-EU citizen is fee-paying or that a Danish address alone grants a tuition exemption.

claim: AU publishes historical 2026/27 annual tuition of EUR 13,000 for Cognitive Science and both business paths, and EUR 17,300 for the three computing degrees.
excerpt: Structured restatement of 2026/2027 table, annual fee for 60 ECTS: Cognitive Science EUR 13,000; Economics and Business Administration (Aarhus and Herning) EUR 13,000; Computer Science, Data Science and IT Product Development EUR 17,300. This is not a published 2027/28 fee schedule.

claim: Quota 1 ranks by first qualifying-exam GPA; quota 2 combines relevant-subject grades and documented relevant qualifications, without requiring prior work experience.
excerpt: Structured restatement: quota 1 admits in descending GPA order from the first completed qualifying examination. Quota 2 assesses relevant-subject GPA and relevant qualifications; activities normally total 4–12 months and must be documented by 15 March. Candidates without relevant qualifications are still assessed on quota 2 GPA. References and personal statements are not relevant qualifications. Page revised 1 October 2026.

claim: IB English meeting Danish B can satisfy AU’s English requirement; otherwise an accepted English test is needed.
excerpt: Structured restatement: English at Danish B level may be met with an assessed English subject in the IB diploma programme. English-medium IB study without an accepted English subject is not a blanket exemption. For English B AU accepts IELTS Academic 6.5 overall with 6.0 each section; TOEFL taken after 21 January 2026 4.5 overall with 4.0 each section (older test 83 overall/20 each); Cambridge C1 Advanced grades A/B/C or 180 points, or B2 First grade A/180. Tests must be verifiable online; upload result and registration receipt by the applicable deadline.

publisher: Aarhus University – Bachelor programmes in English
claim: AU lists five English bachelor subjects and six campus offerings, with an anticipated 2027 Danish-language switch for Cognitive Science.
excerpt: Structured restatement: Cognitive Science, IT Product Development, Economics and Business Administration (Aarhus and Herning), Computer Science and Data Science. Cognitive Science is explicitly flagged as anticipating a change from English to Danish in 2027. The landing page is revised 16 October 2026.

claim: Cognitive Science is currently English but its 2027 teaching language and associated Danish requirement are not yet confirmed.
excerpt: Structured restatement: AU expects the programme to switch from English to Danish for the 2027 intake. If that happens, both Danish A and English B would be required. AU expects the change around 1 December 2026 and directs applicants to this page for updates. The current page still labels instruction English.

publisher: Danish Agency for Higher Education and Science
claim: The Danish agency lists Aarhus Universitet among Denmark’s self-governing universities.
excerpt: Structured restatement: under Selvejende videregående uddannelsesinstitutioner / Universiteter, Aarhus Universitet is one of the listed universities.

claim: AU reports 37,500 students in its 2025 key statistics.
excerpt: Structured restatement: 2025 key statistics report 37,500 students including bachelor, master, PhD and part-time students, across five faculties. This is a dated rounded figure, not a headcount for 2027.

claim: AU has its main campus in Aarhus and additional campuses and research locations; the English first-year offerings listed here are in Aarhus and Herning.
excerpt: Structured restatement: AU lists the main Aarhus campus plus Emdrup, Viborg and Herning campuses, and Roskilde and Flakkebjerg locations. The six relevant programme pages identify Aarhus or Herning as place of study. Other institutional locations must not be presented as campuses for those English offerings.

publisher: Danish Agency for Higher Education and Science – Course Results FAQ
claim: National guidance expressly excludes GSK from raising Course Results to university-entry qualification level; AU’s own page still mentions GSK.
excerpt: Structured restatement of questions 4–5: Course Results qualification supplementation is two subsequent subject-level raises through HF-enkeltfag or self-study, at least one to A; two raises to B suffice if another non-Danish A-level subject is already held. GSK cannot raise the general qualification level; it addresses specific subject deficiencies for an already qualifying award. AU’s IB page still mentions GSK in the qualification-supplement section, so confirm the route and follow the national recognition rule.
interpretation: The national recognition authority excludes GSK from raising the qualification itself, while AU's IB page lists it alongside HF-enkeltfag in its Course Results route. Preserve both readings and the stricter national qualification distinction; do not claim GSK alone qualifies Course Results for university entry. Applicants must confirm their individual route with AU; this conflict remains unresolved pending updated source guidance.

publisher: Aarhus University – Economics and Business Administration (Herning), Danish page
claim: Herning's Danish programme page publishes a 6.0 qualifying-examination average floor for quota 1.
excerpt: Karakterkrav på mindst 6,0 i kvote 1. Structured restatement: applicants below that qualifying-examination average must apply through quota 2 by 15 March noon. The programme is English-taught in Herning. Page revised 27 October 2026.
interpretation: The English programme page omits this floor; omission does not establish an exemption. Retain the existing quota-1-only requirement. The source gives current rules without a 2027-specific year; recheck for the intake. Earlier English-page evidence and source history are preserved.

attestation.note: Opened the exact Danish programme page once to resolve the independent critic's source-note finding. No independent verification claimed.
